newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian banks merger speculation boosts Bel-20.
newsitem.headline: Belgian banks merger speculation boosts Bel-20.

text.p: Belgium's Bel-20 index jumped to a record high on Thursday, driven by lingering merger speculation in the banking sector, a strong dollar and solid Wall Street, dealers said.
The Bel-20 set a record 2,233.65 intraday high en route to a historical closing high of 2,223.49, up 0.65 percent or 14.46 points.
Dealers expected the Bel-20 to remain firm on Friday on the back of low market rates, the dollar and continued speculation that Kredietbank or Generale Bank might be seeking a major cooperation deal.
Kredietbank closed 1.2 percent higher at 13,175 francs and Generale Bank added 0.9 percent at 14,500.
"Unfortunately Dexia is not in the Bel-20, it could have dragged the index a bit lower," one trader said.
Bank Dexia CC fell four percent to 3,480 francs on surprise news of a new stock offering by its controlling shareholder and as a result of arbitrage against shares in French partner bank Dexia CLF.
"The fact that it wants more of its shares to be traded is already an indication that it is too expensive," analyst Patrick Millecam at Antwerp brokerage Corluy & Co said.

Shipping group CMB was one of four Bel-20 stocks to end in the red, shedding 0.8 percent at 2,580, after details of 1996 results published at the weekend showed CMB's 1996 profit to be more disappointing than preliminary figures had indicated.
"Investors are finally realising that current earnings included quite a few exceptionals," one trader said.
Retailer Colruyt gained 1.2 percent at 14,600 on Belgian newspaper reports it had increased its market share in Belgium. It had been the leading gainer for most of the day, touching 14,975.

"They admit competition (in the retail sector) is extrememly tough and market share can only be increased by opening new shops," Millecam said. "But among retailers Colruyt is of course still primus inter pares."
Fellow retailers GIB and Delhaize ended 0.6 percent lower at 1,565 and unchanged at 1,820 respectively.

Millecam said Corluy was sticking to its 1997 forecast of 2,300 points for the Bel-20. Investors continued to put liquidity in the market. "They know they miss out on profits for each percent (of liquidity) that is not invested."
Dealers said that at present the only danger came from the United States.
"From an historical point of view, compared with rates, the Bel-20 is not yet expensive. But Wall Street is expensive," Millecam said.
